issues.problem: The allowlist cues are too loose, so ordinary uses of ambiguous names are credited and can tick matrix features. (a) Version: any bare decimal after the name ('Continue 2.5 miles', 'Factory 4.0'). (b) Head noun: any following IDE/app/tool/editor/assistant/Code/Platform/Cloud/AI word counts, whatever comes before ('the Director app', 'Director Assistant', 'the Cursor tool in Photoshop', 'Linear Code', 'Factory Code'). (c) Vendor list: a generic lead word anywhere earlier in the sentence (solutions, candidates, players, rivals, alternatives, products, competitors) plus a join counts ('Common solutions include Linear Regression ...'). (d) List with a product: any non-ambiguous product in a comma/and/or list counts, even when the member is a phrase ('Open Claude Code or Continue reading', 'Learn GSD and Linear algebra', 'We use BMAD, Sweep the floors'). 24 sentences that 75f40b0 rejected are now credited.

issues.suggested_fix: Version: only 'v<digits>' or a dotted version directly after the name and not followed by a unit word (miles, km, lines) or a lower-case noun. Head noun: credit only when the name is not preceded by a determiner or a capitalised role word, and drop the generic heads Code/Platform/Cloud/AI/Teams for names that are English words (keep IDE/CLI/extension/plugin). Vendor list: only the pack's vendor-list regexes (_MATRIX_LEADERS_RE, _CORE_SET_CLAIM_RE) or leaders/competitors/vendors/APOs in a lead clause that ends in ':' or 'are/include', and the member must be the name alone (optionally with a cue), so 'Linear Regression' and 'Linear equations' fail. List with a product: the same whole-item requirement. Pin all fp7 sentences in the corpus.

issues.problem: The r4 directive was that silver bullet, augment code, open interpreter and the other ambiguous names count only with an explicit product cue. The repair instead exempts PROPER_PHRASES from cues: Title Case alone is enough when the phrase is not after a capitalised word or a determiner and not followed by one. Sentence-initial or after a lower-case preposition, the stock phrases are credited. silver-bullet is a real matrix slug.
issues.evidence: fp7.py: 'Silver Bullet thinking rarely survives contact with legacy code.' -> silver-bullet; 'Silver Bullet solutions do not exist in software.' -> silver-bullet; 'Open Interpreter mode lets the Python shell evaluate lines.' -> open-interpreter; 'Augment Code reviews with a checklist, the guide says.' -> augment-cosmos; 'Spec Kit cars race at the county fair.' -> spec-kit; 'Magic Dev tricks amazed the crowd.' -> magic-dev; 'We welcomed them with Open Hands.' and 'Open Hands make friends, said the poster.' -> openhands.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat PROPER_PHRASES like the other ambiguous names: require a cue (a product verb right after it, a head noun, a version or domain, or a vendor list), or at least require a finite product verb directly after the phrase ('Silver Bullet enforces/ships/provides').
